findings.title: GitHub user verification is bypassed when Integration record does not yet exist
findings.body: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, if `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `Integration.DoesNotExist` (lines 481-482), the view immediately calls `pipeline.next_step()`, skipping the `github_authenticated_user == integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` check on lines 501-505. Because the `Integration` record is only created either asynchronously via the GitHub `installation.created` webhook or at the end of the pipeline in `finish_pipeline()` -> `build_integration()`, two problems occur: (1) during a normal in-app installation flow where the redirect from GitHub arrives before the webhook is processed (or if webhooks are delayed), the `Integration` row does not exist yet and no user validation is performed at all; and (2) an attacker who learns or guesses a victim's `installation_id` before the webhook is processed—or for an installation whose `Integration` record was deleted or never created via webhook—can bind that `installation_id` to their own Sentry organization without being the user who installed the GitHub App.

findings.title: Querying Integration by external_id without provider filter can raise MultipleObjectsReturned or match another provider
findings.body: `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` on line 478 (and again on line 494) does not filter by `provider=GitHubIntegrationProvider.key` (i.e. `"github"`). `Integration` uniqueness is defined on `(provider, external_id)`, not `external_id` alone. If another integration provider (such as `github_enterprise` or any other provider using numeric IDs) has an `Integration` with the same `external_id`, `get()` will either raise `Integration.MultipleObjectsReturned` (causing an unhandled 500 error) or match the wrong provider's integration.

findings.title: KeyError when existing Integration metadata does not contain 'sender'
findings.body: Line 503 accesses `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` directly. However, `build_integration` (lines 376-377) only sets `metadata["sender"]` if `state.get("sender")` is truthy, which is only populated when the integration is created via the installation webhook. Any `Integration` record created previously via the setup pipeline (or whose `sender` key is missing) will not have `"sender"` in `integration.metadata`, causing an unhandled `KeyError` when `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` runs.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests a 404 from GitHub's installation endpoint
findings.body: In `test_installation_not_found`, the test starts by requesting `self.setup_path` instead of `self.init_path` (line 386) and then passes a hardcoded `state` (`ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05`) on line 392 that does not match the pipeline signature (`9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3`). As a result, `OAuthLoginView` fails early on the OAuth `state` mismatch check (line 412 of `integration.py`) and returns `"Invalid installation request."`, never advancing to `GitHubInstallation` or `build_integration` where the mocked 404 response for `/app/installations/{installation_id}` would actually be hit.
